title: Non-Kirchhoff, Chiral and Quantized Thermal Emissivity of Laser-Driven Rotating Conductors
content: We derive the infrared thermal emissivity of a metallic disk that rotates while being illuminated by a chopped, circularly polarized laser beam. In this out-of-equilibrium state a self-induced Barnett field and the Righi–Leduc effect make the thermal conductivity anisotropic and quantized by the azimuthal index m of the helical thermal wave. Assuming the Wiedemann–Franz law for every tensor component and a linear Lorentz–Drude relation between the dielectric and the electrical conductivity tensors, we obtain a gyrotropic dielectric tensor whose anisotropy is quantized in m and whose gyrotropy is odd in the angular velocity. At normal incidence this tensor produces a quantized linear dichroism and a chiral circular dichroism of the absorptivity, but it cannot by itself violate Kirchhoff’s law. A violation follows when the Joule power is compensated by the power of the dynamic chiral Thomson effect: the emitted power is then fixed by the energy balance of the thermal wave rather than by the dissipative part of the dielectric tensor. We give the resulting non-Kirchhoff emissivity, its chiral Righi–Leduc correction and a measurable criterion for the violation, with estimates for iron near the Curie temperature and for bismuth.
